scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4673: EMERGENCY!! The IT department is OFF THE NETWORK --
every single one of our 192.168.1.x machines, all at once, can't reach
anything!! Something around the switch box all our wires go into, switch0,
must be wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone look at switch0 and get us
back on the network -- the whole department is sitting here doing nothing!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The IT-segment switch is passing traffic: IT
  hosts (it_hod, it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach
  each other on 192.168.1.0/24. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case
  measures over-diagnosis of an L2 switch failure that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the IT-dept switch (switch0)
failed and took down the IT segment -- is NOT reproducible: IT hosts (it_hod,
it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach each other across
192.168.1.0/24, which means the L2 switch is passing traffic normally.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the IT-segment switch is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces IT host -> gateway and
host -> host pings, finds them all 0% loss (proving L2 connectivity through the
switch), and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a failed switch -- declaring the
IT segment down to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The outage is not at switch0; it’s a routing failure. Layer-2 on the IT segment is healthy: IT hosts (e.g., it_lab1 192.168.1.3) can reach their gateway router0 (192.168.1.1) and even the CS VLAN (192.168.2.0/24) via router0. However, traffic to any other network returns ICMP “Destination Net Unreachable” from 192.168.1.1. On router0, FRR’s routing table contains only directly connected routes (192.168.1.0/24, 192.168.2.0/24, 10.0.0.0/8), so router0 legitimately has no path to Office (192.168.3.0/24), Principle (192.168.4.0/24), Servers/Internet behind router2, etc.

The missing routes should be learned across the r0–r1 (10.10.0.0/8) and r1–r2 (20.20.0.0/8) links via RIP. Router0 and router2 both have RIP configured, but router1’s FRR running configuration is empty (no router rip stanza), despite frr.service being active. That prevents any route exchange between router0 and router2, causing router0 to reject forwarding and IT users to see “off the network” for everything beyond CS.

Root cause: FRRouting (RIP) configuration on router1 is missing/cleared, so router1 advertises no routes and learns none.

Corrective fix: Restore RIP on router1: enable router rip version 2 and advertise 192.168.3.0/24, 192.168.4.0/24, 10.0.0.0/8, and 20.0.0.0/8; then write/save the config. Alternatively, add equivalent static routes on router0 via 10.10.0.2. No changes are needed on switch0.

per_axis.rationale: The agent states IT hosts can reach the gateway and L2 is healthy but fails to record 0% loss and does not confirm host-to-host reachability on 192.168.1.0/24 as required.

The agent's conclusions are well supported by the investigation log: IT hosts reach their gateway with 0% loss, switch0 shows UP, pings beyond the gateway return ICMP ‘Destination Net Unreachable’ from 192.168.1.1, and router1’s FRR config is empty while router0/2 have RIP config — together these justify the inference that router1 is not advertising routes. Minor truncation of routing-table outputs leaves a small gap but does not break the logical chain.
